figures.first_seen: a bird in flight (or perhaps a fish), with a square and a small triangle dangling loose below it
figures.name: a bird flying right, wing raised behind, tail down, one foot hanging
figures.how: I moved the square Q up onto the body behind the medium triangle to make the head, and turned and moved the small triangle S2 from the tail end to the front of the head as a downward-hooked beak. The raised parallelogram then reads as the wing, the large triangle L1 as the tail and S1 as a foot.
figures.seen_before: unsure: bird-in-flight tangrams are common, but I did not set out to copy one and do not know this exact arrangement

figures.first_seen: a zigzag running down to a point, like a lightning bolt, with little flags sticking off its sides
figures.name: a lightning bolt
figures.how: I moved the parallelogram P and the small triangle S2, which stuck out on the right, onto the upper left of the large triangle L2, so the top becomes a broad block and the left edge steps in like a bolt's zigzag. The small triangle S1 on the left was left where it fell as a spark-like nub.
figures.seen_before: unsure: the zigzag bolt is a familiar symbol, but I do not know of this tangram arrangement

figures.first_seen: two triangular sails, like a sailing boat, above a jumble of pieces
figures.name: a camel lowering its head to drink
figures.how: I lowered the large triangle L2 onto the top of L1 so it sits on the back as the hump, and moved the small triangle S2 into the hole in front of the hump to smooth the neck line. The parallelogram is the neck sloping down to the square head, with L1 and M as the hind and front legs.
figures.seen_before: no: I have not seen this arrangement before; the reading is weaker than the other two, and a viewer may not see a camel without being told
